items.text: CNN reports the departures of Quiñones, Eisenberg and Dhillon from Justice Department leadership; Dhillon left November 5.
items.context: CNN attributes pressure on Quiñones to sources. Actual departures are distinct from reported reasons. Successors, acting appointments and the future of investigations remain unverified.
items.rationale: NET EFFECT (my reading): departures remove particular enforcement managers and give Blanche an opening to consolidate departmental control. They do not terminate investigations or prove a policy retreat. His institution retains investigative authority.
items.fxnote: No fx: personnel turnover and a potential departmental-control shift, not established faction-wide policy reversal.
items.precedent: Nixon’s 1973 Justice Department turnover illustrates how personnel and institutional investigations can diverge; legal circumstances and removal mechanisms differ.

challenge.reading: Blanche may gain managerial room while the maximalist program survives through acting replacements. Departures need not mean moderation, and former officials remain oversight targets.

items.text: CNN reports FBI agents served Alaska Senate candidate Gerald Heikes with a grand-jury subpoena on the Saturday before the election.
items.context: CNN reviewed the subpoena and interviewed Heikes. It sought records concerning recruitment and political groups. Heikes denied being an operative; Peltola denied knowledge. This is an investigative demand, not proof of an unlawful scheme, an indictment or a result in the separate ballot-count case.
items.rationale: My reading: a criminal investigative channel continued alongside failed ballot litigation. Its existence does not establish a successful prosecution or altered count.
items.fxnote: No fx: investigative demand with no verified outcome.

items.text: Some health-policy activists seek cooperation with Democrats after Republican losses.
items.context: CNN reports that activists associated with Make America Healthy Again are discussing cooperation on food and environmental policy. The movement includes people with different views on vaccines and party loyalty. Outreach does not establish that voters have changed parties or that Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has left office. Democrats could gain partners on specific policies without accepting the movement’s full agenda.
items.rationale: My reading: cooperation offers Democrats a way to divide part of Trump’s coalition by policy priority; the size and durability of any electoral transfer remain unknown.
items.fxnote: No fx: policy outreach does not establish a voter transfer or a change in executive authority.
